issues.body: Section 4 states the actual requirement as `nominal_lifetime > 90 min + (pre-flight → container start)`, but the verdict text says only a lifetime under approximately 90 minutes kills the increment and the table marks `~90 min – 2 h` viable. At 90 minutes, or slightly above it but below 90 minutes plus the measured startup margin, a maximum-length worker necessarily expires before completion. The table is the decision seam implementers are told to follow, so its weaker threshold can authorize a liveness regression even though the correct formula appears immediately above it.
issues.fix_hint: Make all three statements use one measurable threshold. Define the required minimum as 90 minutes plus a conservatively measured or explicitly bounded pre-flight-to-container-start margin; abandon at or below that threshold, and begin the viable middle band only above it. If the margin is not yet known, add it to the gating measurement and keep feasibility unresolved rather than approximating it away.
issues.title: Lifetime outcome table drops the required pre-flight margin

verdict.summary: The prior-round major is resolved: the parent record now says M1a can only confirm feasibility, an inconclusive M1a requires the networked M1b after M3, and lack of authorization leaves feasibility unresolved. One consequential decision-rule contradiction remains in the new record. Section 4 correctly derives that a fresh token must outlive 90 minutes plus pre-flight-to-container-start delay, but its outcome table labels the band beginning at approximately 90 minutes as viable and the surrounding text abandons only lifetimes below approximately 90 minutes. A token at or only marginally above 90 minutes cannot satisfy the stated maximum-run requirement once pre-flight delay is included. Because this table is the binding measurement-to-decision seam, it can incorrectly authorize increment 2. Progress is regressing under the required scale because this is a newly recorded major finding, despite the prior finding being fixed.
